column1: # Case table for substrate/.github/workflows/rust-binary-release.yml
# TAB-separated: <name> <context k=v;k=v> <expect-run csv> <expect-skip csv>
# WHAT THIS PINS
# rust-binary-release has two modes, chosen by the boolean input artifact-only
# (default false).
#   default        every leg attaches its own files to the tag's GitHub
#                  Release as soon as it finishes. That behaviour belongs to
#                  7+ callers (mado, tatara-lisp, gen, ...) and must not move.
#   artifact-only  every leg uploads a workflow artifact and publishes nothing.
#                  `artifact-set` merges them once every leg and the linux
#                  baseline are green, and its name is the workflow's
#                  `artifact-name` output. The caller publishes from that.
# Row 1 is the default: build and linux-baseline run, artifact-set does not.
# If artifact-set lost its `if:`, every existing caller would grow a job and a
# merged artifact it never asked for, and this row would report RAN.
# Row 2 is artifact-only: all three jobs run. It also pins that the mode still
# BUILDS and still runs the baseline gate. Putting `!inputs.artifact-only` on
# linux-baseline would make it NOT-RUN here, and would also take artifact-set
# down with it, since artifact-set needs linux-baseline.
# WHAT THIS CANNOT PIN. Whether a GitHub Release is written is decided by STEP
# conditions inside `build`, and step conditions are below this linter's
# resolution. tools/artifact-only-guard.tlisp pins that half: every step that
# writes a GitHub Release must carry `!inputs.artifact-only` as a top-level
# conjunct. It runs next to this table in job-selection-selftest.yml.
# No row models a failed build leg. The linter treats a needed job as "ran"
# once it is selected, so failure is outside what it can express; the skip on
# failure comes from GitHub's implicit success() on `needs:`.
default-tag-push
artifact-only
